_comment: Mutation testing for the Teams bot: caller resolution, the caller-substitution pass, the card renderer, the conversation log, the one round of clarification state, language detection, the turn orchestration, and the bot's own authentication. WHY THESE FILES: every failure in this feature is silent and points the wrong way. Caller resolution answering for the wrong person, a substitution that leaves `@me` in a definition (so the report matches nothing and reads as 'you have no direct reports'), a row cap off by one, a scope caveat that stops appearing on a directory-wide answer to a question that said 'my', a permission check that accepts the wrong permission, a pending clarification that is answered twice -- each produces a perfectly formatted card that a manager will believe. There is no scope filter behind any of this in v1 (see teamsbot/caller.js), so the card IS the control. EXCLUDED, with reasons below: the two files that are Teams glue rather than logic. MUTATOR SET: StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral disabled, matching the sibling API configs -- so the reply wording in text.js and the SQL strings are not mutated; what text.js is actually measured on is detectLanguage and the key-parity check in text.test.js. Run: cd app/api && npm run test:mutation:teamsbot NOT YET MEASURED: this config ships with the feature; `break` is deliberately absent until a first run measures a score (a floor invented without a measurement is either slack or a red run on day one). Add `{ pkg: api, name: teamsbot, label: 'API Teams bot' }` to .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml once it is measured, and set the floor a few points under what it reports.

mutationExclusions.src/teamsbot/handler.js: Teams routing, not logic. Since the OAuthPrompt rewrite this file only decides WHICH turns go where: help is answered inline, every other message and both signin/* invokes are handed to the dialog, membersAdded gets the welcome, and dialog state is saved at the end of a turn. Those are assertions about routing, and they are made directly against the Bot Framework TestAdapter in handler.test.js with a spy dialog -- a mutant that stopped handing an invoke to the dialog fails there. What the bot decides moved to signInDialog.js and service.js, which ARE mutated.
mutationExclusions.src/routes/teamsBot.js: Wiring, not logic: it constructs the CloudAdapter from environment variables, memoises it, and hands the request to it. Every rule it applies is a middleware declared one line at a time -- requirePermission, requireFeature, and their ORDER -- and the order is what actually matters here (permission first, so a disabled bot cannot be discovered by a caller without permission). That is asserted directly, against a real Express app with auth enabled, in src/routes/teamsBot.test.js; a mutant that swapped the two would be caught there rather than by mutating the adapter construction around them.
mutationExclusions.src/teamsbot/log.js: A one-line re-export of nlreports/conversations.js since migration 071 moved the store where both front ends share it. The store itself is mutated in stryker.reports.config.json; there is no statement here for a mutant to change.
